cues.text: Night comes early under the pines. Where the trail forks at a great dead stump, the dark is total for anyone without elven or dwarven eyes.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: I can't see my own feet. Big Man, are my feet still there?

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Both of them. Stop treading on my heels.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Which way did they go? It all looks like the inside of a sack.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Three trails. Ground's too trampled to tell.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Then we need better eyes than ours. Give me an hour.
Ilsevel kneels by the stump with her spellbook, a pinch of incense and a little brass dish of charcoal. The ritual takes most of an hour.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Eleven trees. Twelve. Something moving, east. Gone.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Big Man. You're counting trees.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Somebody has to.
The charcoal flares blue. When the light fades, a small brown owl is sitting beside the stump, blinking at her.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Hello. I have read about familiars for thirty years. You are smaller than the diagrams.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Pell. Your name is Pell.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: He's beautiful, Ilsevel.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Hello, little feathers. Who's a handsome owl, then?

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Pell says you smell of cards and onions. I am paraphrasing. He was ruder.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: He loves me. I can tell.
Ilsevel turns away to put her spellbook back in her satchel, and takes rather longer over it than she needs to.
The north trail opens into a clearing ringed with pale birches. Nothing moves. Nothing sings.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Too open. Too quiet. Don't like it.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Pell. Up, please. Show me.
Pell lifts into the birches. Ilsevel closes her eyes and, for the first time in her life, sees through someone else's.
It is like reading a page while someone spins the book. Branches. Sky. A pale blur that turns out to be her own face.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: I see trees. Sky. Myself, upside down. I do not know which way is...
The first grey shape is already out of the birches, low and fast.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Wolves! Three of them. Get behind me!

battle_narration.text: The lead wolf is across the clearing before anyone has drawn steel.
A pane of blue light snaps up in front of Ilsevel, and the wolf's teeth close on nothing.
The last wolf comes in fast and low at Tamsin. She never sees it. She goes down hard and stays down.
Ilsevel scrambles up out of the grass and grabs the nearest wolf by the scruff. The lightning does the rest.
Brannoc's sword comes down once, hard. One wolf left.
Oriel says one word, and Tamsin's eyes open.

cues.text: Then the clearing is quiet again. The right kind of quiet, this time.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Tamsin. Sit. Let me see that bite.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: It's nothing. I once lost an argument with a duke's hound. This is a scratch.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: You went down and didn't get up. Humour me.
Ilsevel kneels where the wolves fell. Their ribs show through their coats, and the tips of their fur have no colour in them at all.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Starved, and far from wherever they belong. And look at the fur. It has gone grey at the tips. Not old. Drained.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Like the grass at Lantern Thirty-Seven. Something drove them out of the deep woods.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Then we're walking toward it.
Wings, then a small weight beside Ilsevel. Pell has come back down from the birches.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: You came back.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: East, then? Toward the something?

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: East. Quiet. Single file.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Pell says he will go first. He says he is the only one of us with any sense.
